specs.value: Volcanic soil substrate for freshwater planted and shrimp aquariums
Mineral-rich volcanic soil from the foothills of Mount Aso, Japan
Supports neutral to slightly acidic pH
Light, porous, non-compacting; nitrifying bacteria can colonise it
Does not discolour water; helps control tannin staining from driftwood
Fluval brand (Canada), made and packed in Japan (according to the seller)
Contains dormant beneficial bacteria that activate in water to help start the nitrogen cycle and lower ammonia in new tanks
Planted tanks; can be the main substrate in small tanks or a top layer in large ones

fits.fact: Made for planted aquariums and shrimp tanks; the granules give newborn shrimp somewhere to hide
The slightly acidic, neutral pH suits most tropical plants, fish and shrimp
A Vietnamese seller says it suits plants from mosses and ferns to carpeting plants such as Monte Carlo and hairgrass
Not recommended with fish that dig in the substrate, such as African cichlids and catfish

usage.fact: Do not rinse it. Fill the tank slowly; if the water turns cloudy, run the filter for 24–48 hours
Lay it about 3–5 cm deep. One shop advises 5–8 cm
Plants can go in on the first day. Add root tabs for heavy root feeders after 2–3 weeks, and liquid fertiliser after about 2 weeks
Wait 3–5 days before adding a few hardy animals. A bacteria starter can shorten cycling to about 5–7 days
To reduce cloudiness, pour water onto a container placed on the soil. Do not vacuum it like gravel. Prefer small water changes (10–15%, once or twice a week)
If cloudiness lasts past 48 hours, change 10% of the water daily for 1–2 days. Fine filter wool also helps
Plan to replace it every 2–3 years, as its nutrients run out
For cloudiness after setup, one shop suggests 30–50% daily water changes for the first few days plus fine filter wool

issues.fact: Users report cloudy water lasting more than a day, and black clouds whenever the substrate is disturbed
The granules are light and break easily. Rinsing or vacuuming turns them to mud, and plants can be hard to anchor
Light granules make cleaning harder, and small balls can clog siphons
Some reviewers saw no difference in shrimp health compared with other substrates
Bio-Stratum adds dormant bacteria for a faster cycle; plain Stratum does not. Some Vietnamese shop pages mix up the two (the Bích Phương Stratum page describes dormant microbes)
The Bích Phương category page shows 85,000₫ for 'Fluval Stratum 8KG', which is actually the 1 kg repack price. Confirm the size before buying
Vietnamese sellers' pH claims (stable 6.5–6.8) are unverified

alternatives.why: Same volcanic soil with added dormant bacteria to start cycling faster; sold in Vietnam for about 607,000–650,000₫
A cheaper, inert clay-type substrate (about 265,000₫ at Bích Phương); it does not turn to mud but adds no nutrients
A premium nutrient soil for planted tanks (790,000₫ at Bích Phương, out of stock when checked)
A Japanese soil at a similar price (550,000₫) for planted and shrimp tanks
